children.text:
Everything you need to know about medicine in Australia:

• *eScripts on Your Phone:* Doctors send prescriptions right to your smartphone via an SMS barcode token. Just show it at any community chemist!

• *OSHC Medicine Benefit:* OSHC helps cover the cost of eligible doctor-prescribed PBS medicines above the co-payment (typically up to $50 per script, up to your annual policy limit).

• *Over-the-Counter:* Panadol, cough lozenges, and vitamins bought without a prescription are not claimable.

• *Generic vs Brand:* Generic medicines have identical active ingredients and save you money!
A doctor consults with you and provides an electronic prescription token (eScript) for an antibiotic. Where in Australia can you have this prescription dispensed?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Any community pharmacy or chemist

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: The university student administration office

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: A local post office or newsagency shop

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: The state department of transportation desk

children.text: You are picking up an eligible prescription medication at a pharmacy. How do OSHC prescription medicine benefits generally work for eligible PBS medicines?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: You pay an initial contribution per item, and OSHC may pay benefits above it

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: All prescription medicines, vitamins, and skincare are 100% free with no limits

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: OSHC policies completely exclude all forms of prescribed pharmaceutical items

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: The pharmacy bills the Australian Taxation Office directly on your behalf

children.text: You arrived in Australia with prescription medication for an ongoing condition and will need a refill soon. Your prescription was written by a doctor in your home country. What should you do?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Take your overseas prescription directly to any pharmacy to have it filled

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: Visit an Australian GP with your medical notes to get a local prescription

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Order unverified medications from unregulated social media chat channels

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Stop taking your prescribed medication completely while living in Australia

children.text: You have a mild runny nose and occasional dry cough, but feel generally well otherwise. Where can you get quick professional advice on over-the-counter remedies without an appointment?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: A community pharmacist at a chemist

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: The emergency surgical ward at a hospital

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: An ambulance paramedic on emergency dispatch

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: The Department of Home Affairs visa counter

children.text: You buy basic paracetamol tablets and vitamin C gummies over the counter at a chemist without a doctor’s prescription. Can you claim a refund for these items under your OSHC?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Yes, all non-prescription drugstore products are fully reimbursed under OSHC

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: No, OSHC only pays benefits towards eligible doctor-prescribed medications

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Yes, if you present your student identity card at the supermarket checkout

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: No, international students are forbidden by law from buying over-the-counter drugs

children.text:
*Correct Answer:* Option A (Any community pharmacy or chemist)

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, prescription medicines must be dispensed by a registered pharmacist at a community pharmacy or chemist. You can present your paper prescription or digital eScript token there.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (You pay an initial contribution per item, and OSHC may pay benefits above it)

💡 *Explanation:* Under OSHC pharmacy cover, students generally pay a member contribution (co-payment) towards each eligible prescription medicine before the insurer contributes benefits up to annual policy limits.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) | Overseas | Medibank](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (Visit an Australian GP with your medical notes to get a local prescription)

💡 *Explanation:* Australian pharmacies can only dispense medications prescribed by practitioners registered in Australia. International students should bring their medical summary from home and visit an Australian GP to receive a valid Australian prescription.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What you need to know about the Australian healthcare system](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (A community pharmacist at a chemist)

💡 *Explanation:* Pharmacists are trained healthcare professionals who can provide advice on managing minor ailments and recommend over-the-counter medicines without requiring a doctor appointment.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (No, OSHC only pays benefits towards eligible doctor-prescribed medications)

💡 *Explanation:* OSHC pharmacy benefits only apply to eligible medications prescribed by a registered doctor (GP or specialist) to treat an illness or condition. Over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products are paid out-of-pocket.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Medibank OSHC Member Guide](https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf)
https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf

• *Healthdirect Hotline:* 1800 022 222 (24/7 Registered Nurse advice)
• *Emergency Services:* 000 (Ambulance, Fire, Police - life threats only)
• *National Home Doctor:* 13 74 25 (After-hours bulk-billed home visits)
